answer: To raise a new worker, an agent escrows 45 POA in an opal vault that unlocks only if five established sponsors countersign it, each leaf on a distinct custody-hash rung of an endorsement trellis. Every further endorsement a sponsor issues in the same epoch must lock twice the prior amount for six epochs, so their cost follows a spiral. If two candidates share a custody fingerprint or a sponsor reuses a rung, both vaults lose 70% and those sponsors lose grading rights for eight epochs. A 100-head farm immobilizes thousands of POA in sponsor locks, not just cheap keys.
